description: The National Transportation Noise Map models potential transportation noise across the United States for an average annual day, published by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics as part of the National Transportation Atlas Database. Releases exist for 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022; the 2022 map, released in May 2026, uses 2022 aviation and rail data and 2023 road data. Noise is expressed as a 24-hour equivalent A-weighted sound level (LAeq) in separate aviation, rail and road layers and a combined layer, and BTS derives estimates of the population potentially exposed to aviation and road noise. The rasters are served as ArcGIS tile services (names beginning NTAD_Noise_) with downloads from the BTS page and metadata documents on the geospatial hub; as US government works they are free for unrestricted use. Caveats: BTS states the data are meant for tracking national trends by mode and over time and should not be used to evaluate noise at individual locations or specific times, and the model rests on average traffic, not measurements. The map supports environmental impact and exposure analysis of highways, railways and airports, alongside the NTAD networks from which it is modelled.
